questions.prompt: A property's convention-inferred configuration isn't what you want, so you add a Data Annotation attribute to it. Which wins?
options: The convention, because conventions are always applied last
The Data Annotation, because annotations override the conventions
Neither; EF Core reports a conflict at migration time
Whichever is declared first in the class
questions.explanation: Conventions have their limits; Data Annotations let you fine-tune the model, and they override the conventions.

questions.prompt: A dashboard always shows each student with all enrolled courses. Which loading style fits, and how does it fetch the data?
options: Lazy loading: one extra query each time `Courses` is accessed
Explicit loading: call `Load()` for every student in a loop
Eager loading with `Include(s => s.Courses)`: related data comes back as part of the query, using JOINs
Eager loading with `ToList()` alone: EF Core includes every navigation by default
questions.explanation: Eager loading (`Include` / `ThenInclude`) loads related data immediately as part of the query, a single query with JOINs; it suits cases where you know you'll need the related data.

questions.prompt: You installed `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Proxies` and called `UseLazyLoadingProxies()`. What else does the lesson say lazy loading needs?
options: Navigation properties must be declared `virtual`
Every query must end with `Include`
The context must be created with `AsNoTracking()`
Navigation properties must be arrays instead of `ICollection<T>`
questions.explanation: Lazy loading must be enabled: install the Proxies package, call `UseLazyLoadingProxies()` in `OnConfiguring`, and make the navigation properties `virtual`.

questions.prompt: With lazy loading on, this loop prints `s.Courses.Count` for every student loaded by `context.Students.ToList()`. What problem does the lesson warn about?
options: The courses are never loaded, so every count is 0
All courses for every student are loaded in the first query
It throws, because `Courses` must be included first
The N+1 problem: one query for the students plus a separate query per student's courses
questions.explanation: Lazy loading runs a separate query each time a navigation property is first accessed, so a loop over many students causes the N+1 query problem.

questions.prompt: You have already loaded one `student` and now want its courses, but only for this student. Which call does the lesson use?
options: `context.Students.Include(s => s.Courses).Load()`
`context.Entry(student).Collection(s => s.Courses).Load()`
`student.Courses.ToList()` with lazy loading turned off
`context.Entry(student).Reference(s => s.Courses).Include()`
questions.explanation: Explicit loading loads related data manually after the main entity is retrieved, with `.Entry(...).Collection(...).Load()` (or `.Reference(...).Load()` for a single navigation).
